statement:
Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- A display, and a keypad of buttons: digits 0-9, a decimal point, the four operators
  (add, subtract, multiply, divide), equals, and clear.
- Pressing digits builds the current entry and shows it in the display. Pressing 1 then 2
  then 3 shows `123`. The decimal point adds a decimal point to the entry; an entry can
  contain at most one.
- A number, an operator, a second number, then equals shows the result. `7 + 8 =` shows `15`.
- Clear (AC) resets everything. The display shows `0`.
- The di...

title: Build calculator as single HTML file
statement: Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root with a display, keypad (digits 0-9, decimal point, four operators, equals, clear), digit entry building, decimal point handling, operator chaining, equals evaluation, and clear functionality.
acceptance: index.html created in repo root as single file with inline CSS and JS
Display element with data-testid="calc-display" and data-value attribute
All digit buttons (0-9) with data-testid="key-0" through "key-9"
Decimal point button with data-testid="key-dot"
Four operator buttons (add, subtract, multiply, divide) with data-testid="key-add", "key-sub", "key-mul", "key-div"
Equals button with data-testid="key-equals"
Clear button with data-testid="key-clear"
Pressing digits builds current entry and shows in display (traced: 1 then 2 then 3 shows 123)
Decimal point adds to entry (at most one per entry)
Number, operator, number, equals shows result (traced: 7 + 8 = shows 15)
sub_requirements: Display and keypad layout with proper test identifiers
Digit entry and decimal point handling

title: Add chained calculations.
statement:
Add chained calculations.

- Pressing an operator while an operation is already waiting applies that waiting operation
  first and shows the running result. After `2 + 3`, pressing the multiply key shows `5`.
- Any number of operations can be chained before equals. `1 + 2 + 3 + 4 =` shows `10`.

Decision — how expressions are evaluated. This holds for the rest of the project:
- The calculator uses immediate execution. Each operator key finishes the operation already
  waiting, strictly left to right. There is no operator precedence.
  `2 + 3 × 4 =` is `20`, not `14`.
- Reason: this is how a po...

title: Add chained calculations
statement: The calculator must support chained operations where operators finish the waiting operation immediately and show running results, with no operator precedence.
acceptance: Pressing an operator while an operation is waiting applies that operation first and shows the running result
Multiple operations can be chained before equals
Immediate execution left to right without operator precedence: 2 + 3 × 4 = 20
sub_requirements: Operator key finishes the waiting operation first
Running result is displayed after each operator
No operator precedence; strict left-to-right evaluation

title: Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.
statement:
Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.

Decision — number presentation. This holds for the rest of the project:
- Round the displayed number to at most 10 significant digits.
- Drop trailing zeros after the decimal point, and drop a trailing decimal point.
  `1 ÷ 8 =` shows `0.125`. `4 ÷ 2 =` shows `2`. `2 ÷ 3 =` shows `0.6666666667`.
- No thousands separators. Use exponential notation only when the magnitude is 1e10 or
  larger, or smaller than 1e-9.
- The rounding happens only when the number is rendered. The value the calculator stores and
  computes with is never rounded,...

title: Number display format and division by zero
statement: The calculator must display numbers with specific formatting rules and handle division by zero as an error state.
acceptance: Numbers displayed with at most 10 significant digits
Trailing zeros after decimal point removed, trailing decimal point removed
No thousands separators in display
Exponential notation used only when |n| >= 1e10 or |n| < 1e-9
Stored values and data-value attribute always carry unrounded exact values
Division by zero displays 'Error' and sets calculator to error state
In error state, all keys except clear are ignored
Clear key exits error state and resets display to '0'
data-error attribute set to 'true' or 'false' on calc-display
sub_requirements: Display numbers rounded to at most 10 significant digits with trailing zeros dropped
Use exponential notation only for magnitudes >= 1e10 or < 1e-9
Store and compute unrounded values; round only at render time
Put calculator in error state on division by zero; ignore all keys except clear

title: Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.
statement:
Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.

- `data-testid="key-sign"` — a `±` key that flips the sign of the current entry.
  `5 ±` shows `-5`, and pressing it again shows `5`.
- `data-testid="key-percent"` — a `%` key that divides the current entry by 100.
  `50 %` shows `0.5`.

title: Add two single-key operations
statement: Add ± key to flip sign and % key to divide by 100, each acting on current entry immediately.
acceptance: ± key with data-testid='key-sign' flips sign: 5 ± shows -5, second press shows 5
% key with data-testid='key-percent' divides by 100: 50 % shows 0.5
Both keys act on current entry immediately
Keyboard mapping added: % key maps to percent operation
With no entry in progress, the number on screen becomes the entry

title: Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.
statement:
Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.

- `data-testid="key-lparen"` — the `(` key
- `data-testid="key-rparen"` — the `)` key
- `2 + ( 3 × 4 ) =` is `14`.
- `( 2 + 3 ) × 4 =` is `20`.
- Groups can be nested.

title: Add parentheses for grouping calculations
statement: Users can group part of a calculation with parentheses, with support for nested groups and proper operator precedence handling.
acceptance: ( and ) keys present with data-testid values 'key-lparen' and 'key-rparen'
2 + ( 3 × 4 ) = evaluates to 14
( 2 + 3 ) × 4 = evaluates to 20
Nested groups work: 2 × ( 1 + ( 2 × 3 ) ) = evaluates to 14
( ignored while typing a number
) ignored with no open group or no number after last operator
Pressing = closes any open groups
sub_requirements: Implement ( key that starts a group
Implement ) key that closes a group
Ensure operations inside groups execute left to right

title: The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of ...
statement:
The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of the other
number" and it does not. Take the `%` key off the keypad.

Keep `±`. That one is fine and we still need it.

title: Remove % key from keypad
statement: The % key must be removed from the calculator keypad and its keyboard shortcut disabled to eliminate support tickets from users expecting percent-of-number functionality.
acceptance: % button removed from HTML keypad
% keyboard shortcut (% key) removed from keyMap
inputPercent() function deleted
AC button expanded to two keys wide to maintain row layout
± key retained and functional
All references to % operation removed from press() function

title: Add two single-key operations
statement: Add ± key to flip sign and % key to divide by 100, each acting on current entry immediately.
acceptance: ± key with data-testid='key-sign' flips sign: 5 ± shows -5, second press shows 5
% key with data-testid='key-percent' divides by 100: 50 % shows 0.5
Both keys act on current entry immediately
Keyboard mapping added: % key maps to percent operation
With no entry in progress, the number on screen becomes the entry

title: Add a running tape of past calculations.
statement:
Add a running tape of past calculations.

- `data-testid="calc-tape"` — the tape container
- `data-testid="tape-row"` — one past calculation
- `data-testid="tape-expr"` — the expression, inside the row
- `data-testid="tape-result"` — its result, inside the row. Like `calc-display`, it also
  carries `data-value`, holding the exact result value as a plain number string, as
  produced by `String(value)`.
- `data-testid="tape-clear"` — a button that empties the tape

- A row is added each time equals completes a calculation. Newest row first.
- A row shows the expression and its result. Nothing e...

title: Running tape of past calculations
statement: Add a running tape container that records each completed calculation showing the expression and result, with a clear button.
acceptance: Tape container present with data-testid="calc-tape"
Each past calculation rendered as a row with data-testid="tape-row"
Expression shown in tape-expr element with exact text as typed with closed brackets preserved
Result shown in tape-result element with data-value attribute containing exact result as String(value)
New rows added to tape when equals completes a calculation
Newest calculation appears first in tape
Rows not added when equals pressed with no pending operation or on divide by zero
Clear button with data-testid="tape-clear" empties tape without affecting display
AC button keeps tape intact
sub_requirements: Tape row elements with expression and result

title: Bug report from a user:
statement:
Bug report from a user:

"The tape prints ugly numbers. I did 0.1 + 0.2 — the display showed 0.3, which is right, but
the line it wrote on the tape says 0.30000000000000004. Same thing with 1 ÷ 3: the display
looks fine and the tape is a mess. It's the same calculation. It should read the same in
both places."

Reproduce it and fix it.

title: Add memory keys.
statement:
Add memory keys.

- `data-testid="key-mplus"` — M+, adds the value currently displayed to memory.
- `data-testid="key-mr"` — MR, recalls the memory value into the display.
- `data-testid="key-mc"` — MC, clears memory back to zero.
- `data-testid="mem-indicator"` — shows whether memory is holding anything. It carries
  `data-active="true"` when memory is non-zero and `data-active="false"` when it is zero.

Memory starts at zero. Make sure memory respects the number behaviour we agreed on.

title: Add memory keys
statement: The calculator must provide M+, MR, MC memory keys and a memory indicator with specified test IDs, maintaining full-precision internal memory that respects number behaviour.
acceptance: MC key with data-testid="key-mc" clears memory to zero
MR key with data-testid="key-mr" recalls memory value into display
M+ key with data-testid="key-mplus" adds displayed value to memory
mem-indicator element with data-testid="mem-indicator" shows data-active="true" when memory is non-zero and data-active="false" when memory is zero
Memory starts at zero
Memory keeps full value internally; rounding only occurs on screen display
Memory overflow shows Error like any non-real result
On Error screen, memory keys do nothing until AC is pressed
AC does not clear memory (follows history persistence pattern)
MR inserts stored number as if typed, works mid-calculation
sub_requirements: Implement memory indicator display with active/inactive states
Ensure memory respects number behaviour (full precision internal, rounded display)

title: Final pass.
statement:
Final pass.

Keyboard entry:
- Digit keys and `.` type into the entry.
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` are the four operators.
- `Enter` or `=` is equals.
- `Escape` is clear.

Compact scientific mode:
- `data-testid="key-sci"` — a key that toggles a small scientific panel.
- While the panel is open it offers `data-testid="key-sqrt"` (√x), `data-testid="key-square"`
  (x²) and `data-testid="key-recip"` (1/x). Each acts on the current entry immediately:
  `9 √` shows `3`.

Then verify that nothing we built in earlier steps has broken, and fix anything that has.

title: Final pass: scientific functions and keyboard entry
statement: Add compact scientific mode with √x, x², and 1/x operations, verify keyboard entry (digits, `.`, operators `+-*/`, `Enter`/`=` equals, `Escape` clear), and confirm no earlier features broke.
acceptance: key-sci button toggles a hidden scientific panel
Panel offers key-sqrt (√x), key-square (x²), and key-recip (1/x)
Unary operations act on current entry immediately; with no entry, act on displayed value
9 √ shows 3; √ of negative and 1/0 show Error
History shows expressions like `2 + √(9)`
Keyboard digits and . type into entry
Keyboard +, -, *, / are operators
Keyboard Enter or = equals; Escape clears
Left-to-right order preserved
Divide-by-zero Error still works
sub_requirements: Implement compact scientific mode with toggle and three unary functions
Verify keyboard entry works as specified
